_comment: The Grade 2 Computing standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Eleven lessons organised by the strands of Cambridge Primary Computing 0059 Stage 2 (31 objectives), NOT by the units of the Word-pack course under computing/grade-2/data, so progress is written under l01..l11 - see THE UNIT PROBLEM in wire-progress.py. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall. Lesson 11 was split out of lesson 10 by the validation of 2026-09-11 (lesson 10 had grown to 21 steps), so lesson 10's floor went from 6 to 3 and the three it gave up are lesson 11's; lesson 10 keeps its file name so the address the live course knows serves the new lesson.
subject: computing
hubStrands: Algorithms that are precise: following and understanding them, finding and correcting the one step that is wrong, working out which steps a task needs, predicting what an algorithm will produce, and giving instructions exact enough to draw a picture or build a tower.

A program tells the computer how to run an algorithm; building programs with the repeat block; planning the instructions for each object; testing as you go; debugging with a partner; and steering a floor robot to a destination.

Why data is kept on computers; collecting categorical data for a purpose, and the ways of doing it; which questions give statistical data and which do not; presenting data as a graph; and using data to solve a problem.

The devices that can join a network and the internet; two devices doing together what neither can alone; wired and wireless networks; telling when a network is there and when it is not; and what sharing over a network means, including its risks.

Hardware and software, by their proper names; what makes a device easy to use; input devices and output devices; the jobs computers do better than people; choosing a device for the place and the purpose; and robots in stories against robots that work.
